summary.text: James Bush III is the Democratic candidate for Florida House of Representatives District 109, a seat he previously held from 2018 to 2022 and, earlier, from 2008 to 2010.
Ballotpedia lists the November 3, 2026 general election as canceled, with Bush winning the seat without appearing on the ballot.

paragraphs.text: Bush is a teacher, and Ballotpedia lists him as a member of the Community Action Agency Board, chair of the Florida Martin Luther King, Jr. Institute for Nonviolence, and a member of United Teachers of Dade.
James Bush III won election to the Florida House from District 109 in 2008 and ran unopposed in that general election, serving in 2009 and 2010.
During 2009 and 2010, he was assigned to the Government Accountability Act Council, the Health Care Regulation Policy Committee and the Public Counsel Oversight Committee.
He lost the 2012 Democratic primary for Florida State Senate District 39 to Dwight Bullard, finishing third with 27.6% of the vote.
Bush won the 2018 Democratic primary for House District 109 with 53.2% of the vote, defeating Cedric McMinn, and assumed office on November 6, 2018.
He served until November 8, 2022, with committee assignments that included Education and Employment, Collective Bargaining, House Rules and Ethics, and Budget.
Ashley Gantt defeated him in the 2022 Democratic primary, and Gantt defeated him again in the 2024 primary, in which he received 28.8%.
In 2026, Ballotpedia reports that Bush defeated John Taylor, Satin Fye and Broadway Harewood in the Democratic primary for District 109.
